reasoning: JNIM has imposed an economic blockade on Bamako causing severe hardship, but taking control of a city of 3-4 million people is vastly different from maintaining a siege. With only ~6,000 fighters spread across multiple countries, JNIM lacks the force concentration needed to capture and hold such a large urban center. The Malian military, despite weaknesses, has Russian Africa Corps support. Historically, jihadist groups in the Sahel have struggled to hold major cities against determined resistance. The 3-month timeframe is very short for such a dramatic outcome. While the situation is dire, actual capture of Bamako remains unlikely.
